newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS-BASF H1 net income rises to 1.417 bln dmk.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-BASF H1 net income rises to 1.417 bln dmk.

text.p: German chemicals group BASF AG on Thursday reported a 5.8 percent rise in pretax profit to 2.458 billion marks ($1.3 billion) from 2.323 billion, a figure that came in at the lower end of what analysts had forecast.
The group saw first half net income rise 3.4 percent to 1.417 billion marks, while sales grew by 14.5 percent to 27.8 billion marks from 24.3 billion.
As in the other chemical companies, sales were boosted by the weakness of the deutschemark against the dollar.
BASF said its North American sales rose 19.1 percent after conversion to marks, an increase that was "largely influenced" by the rise in the U.S. dollar exchange rate.

"The average rate of (dollar/mark) conversion was 12.8 percent higher than in the same period of 1996," the group said, adding that out of the 14.5 percent growth in sales, currency and conversion contributed 4.2 percent.
The group said its objective of increasing earnings in 1997 and achieving group sales of more than 50 billion marks was within reach.
"Following the customary lull during the vacation period, we expect sales and earnings to continue at a high level in the coming months," BASF said in a statement.
"Strong demand for our products and appropriately full order books confirm these growth expectations.
"At present, we consider our objective of increasing group sales in 1997 to over 50 billion marks and exceeding the previous year's earnings to be within reach."

A poll by analysts before the results forecast pre-tax profit of between 2.46 billion and 2.53 billion marks, up 5.9 to nine percent, and sales growth of 13.3 percent to 14.6 percent -- to 27.5 to 27.8 billion marks.
In early share business BASF was one of the heaviest traded stocks. The share was up 20 pfennigs at 71.70 marks, while the overall market was up 32.83 points at 4,269.89.

BASF said that its health and nutrition unit registered an above average sales increase, principally due to its crop protection business in North America and strengthened by its purchase of Sandoz's corn herbicide business.
Health and nutrition sales were up 19.9 percent at 6.062 billion marks in the first half, but income fell to 678 million from 718 million.
BASF said this was because of repercussions on drug prices of budgetary problems in health systems worldwide, and the high cost of launching new pharmaceuticals.
Plastics and fibres also registered strong sales growth, up 16.6 percent to 6.878 million marks, but earnings fell in this sector to 260 million marks from 457 million.
"Earnings suffered from declining selling prices in some product lines and markets, especially in the case of the polystyrene business in the NAFTA region," BASF said.

Chemical sales rose 15.6 percent to 4.172 billion as cracker capacity in the basic chemicals division was fully utilised. Higher prices and larger volumes resulted in improved earnings, BASF said, with income up to 817 million marks from 750 million.
Earnings in BASF's oil and gas unit rose to 482 million marks from 292 million, while colorants and finishing products income rose strongly to 411 million marks from 175 million.
